- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.
- Model consistently overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period); apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% for 2–3 periods post-spike.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if recent 5-day average is >10% above 30d moving avg, reduce forecast; if below, increase slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- For 30d forecasts, model often fails to capture late-period volatility; add 1–2% upward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or positive in last 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.0 values, model tends to be overly conservative; increase forecast by 1–2% to reflect potential breakout.
